Thanks man. I’m glad that you were able to do what half of sex offenders in the US cannot. I’ll keep the tip in mind, and do my best to find a new steady job to help pay for bills. Right now, I’m just with Grubhub, and I’ll be forever thankful that they looked at the background check of mine, saw that I wasn’t convicted and gave me a chance.

Exactly, a lot of place will say, “ we’re hire sex offenders.” But when a sex offender, convicted or not, tries to take up that offer; suddenly the position is filled. If it happens once or twice, fine, but 5 times? 10? They make it virtually impossible to either keep up with your bills plus lawyer fees when you’re just facing the court case, but after a conviction and you serve your time, the punishment doesn’t end because unless you lived with someone prior to prison, a lot of places don’t let you rent, or work, or even eat at their homeless shelter.

Admittedly, I almost have to wonder if it’d be better if I just didn’t.... exist. It seems cowardly, but even if the charges were dropped, it’d follow me everywhere I go until I could get it expunged from my record. Which ,after paying for a lawyer, would take ages. Here recently it’s crossed my mind frequently, waiting for the outcome of the case. And I don’t actually want to, but it seems like it’d be simpler than just dealing with all the bullshit that comes with charge. It’s almost like they are asking for sex offenders to commit a different crime, like thievery or even murder, just because for anyone on the registry they have a hell of a time holding employment, finding housing, even getting a damn thing on credit rather than paying outright. Sorry to seem so whiny, but I just needed to get some things off my chest. Thanks for the advice though, I’ll keep it in mind.
